instrument: EASA MLEAP final report (Machine Learning Application Approval)
status_note: Non-binding research report by Airbus Protect, LNE, Numalis
clause_or_section_seen: Exec. summary; data completeness, generalisation, robustness tasks
requirement_paraphrase: Uses W-shaped learning assurance; treats ODD and trained model as two pillars for data completeness/representativeness; recommends combining statistical, formal and empirical methods; system-level monitoring should handle model errors and uncertainty.
Asks operators to file AIREPs for GNSS anomalies, report safety-impacting events under Reg (EU) 376/2014 and report suspected spoofing and higher-risk jamming to manufacturers.

instrument: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02 R4 (GNSS outage and alterations)
edition_or_version: Revision 4, 3 July 2026 (replaces R3 of 5 July 2024; first issued 17 Mar 2022)
status_note: Informational bulletin; recommendations not mandatory; further safety/airworthiness directive may follow
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends recurrent training of flight crews and relevant ops personnel; assessing risks of losing onboard GNSS; before flights into known affected areas, ensuring GNSS-backup systems are not MEL-inoperative and MEL backups do not rely on GNSS; planning non-GNSS procedures where practical; verifying position by non-GNSS means and navaid availability (jamming); monitoring non-GNSS navaids/EPU and GNSS vs non-GNSS time (spoofing); using flight data monitoring where required.

instrument: EU AI Act, Annex I (as amended)
edition_or_version: Reg 2024/1689 Annex I as amended by Reg 2026/1744
status_note: Unchanged and still unconfirmed: the Annex I amendment was not reached in the official text (extraction ends before it).
clause_or_section_seen: Annex I Section A item 1 (deleted); Section B item 21
requirement_paraphrase: Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 is listed in Annex I Section B (not Section A) after amendment.

edition_or_version: Reg 2024/1689 as amended by Reg 2026/1744 (text from unofficial reproduction)
status_note: Official: para 1 replaced (refers to Art. 4a(1)), para 5 deleted, para 6 replaced (point (9)). Base paras 2-4 not seen officially; the 'full text seen' access level rests on the unofficial site only.
requirement_paraphrase: Training, validation and testing data need documented governance (sourcing, labelling, cleaning, bias checks, gap identification), must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as error-free as reasonably possible, and take into account the geographic, contextual, behavioural or functional setting of use.
applies_to: High-risk AI systems that train models

instrument: EU AI Act, Art. 11 and Annex IV
status_note: As amended (SME/small mid-cap simplification text appears in two versions on the page)
requirement_paraphrase: Technical documentation must be prepared before placement and kept current; Annex IV elements include design specifications and rationale, training data provenance, human oversight assessment, validation/testing procedures with dated signed test logs, cybersecurity, risk management, lifecycle changes, standards applied, EU declaration of conformity, post-market plan. For Annex I Section A products, one combined document set. Art. 11(1) second subparagraph replaced by 2026/1744 point (10): SMEs and small mid caps may give Annex IV information in a simplified Commission form that notified bodies must accept. Only one version of this wording was seen officially. 'Paragraphs 1 to 3' not verified.

status_note: Recital (40) of 2026/1744 and the Commission news page give 2 Dec 2027 (Art. 6(2) and Annex III) and 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 6(1) and Annex I). The Art. 113 amending article and paragraph were not reached; original dates not confirmed officially.
clause_or_section_seen: Art. 113 (amending article in 2026/1744 not seen); Recital (40) seen
requirement_paraphrase: Chapter III Sections 1-3 (high-risk): Annex III systems from 2 Dec 2027; Annex I (Art. 6(1)) systems from 2 Aug 2028; certain new Art. 5 bans from 2 Dec 2026; Arts. 102-110 from 27 July 2026.

status_note: In force; high-risk obligations apply per B17
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems must technically allow automatic event logging over their lifetime so risk situations, substantial modifications, post-market monitoring and deployer operation can be traced; para 3 specifies minimum logs only for Annex III point 1(a) systems.

edition_or_version: Reg 2024/1689 as amended by Reg 2026/1744 (text from unofficial reproduction)
status_note: In force; high-risk obligations apply per B17
requirement_paraphrase: Instructions for use must state accuracy levels and metrics, robustness, cybersecurity, factors affecting them, foreseeable misuse risks, dataset information, human oversight measures, hardware needs, lifespan and maintenance/update frequency, and log-handling mechanisms.

status_note: In force; high-risk obligations apply per B17
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems must be designed so humans can effectively oversee them; oversight scaled to risk, autonomy and context; overseers must be able to understand limits, notice anomalies and automation bias, override or reverse outputs, and stop the system safely.

status_note: Note: Art. 42, new para 3 (2026/1744 point (18)) presumes Art. 15 cybersecurity compliance for products under Reg 2024/2847 meeting its Art. 12(1) conditions.
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems need appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle; declared accuracy metrics; resilience to errors and faults (redundancy or fail-safe allowed); mitigation of feedback loops for learning systems; protection against data poisoning, adversarial inputs and model flaws.

Documented quality management system covering compliance strategy, design/development/testing procedures, standards used, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring, serious incident reporting, resources and accountability. Art. 17(2) replaced by point (11): implementation proportionate to provider size, keeping the required level of rigour and protection.

status_note: Replaced by 2026/1744 Art. 1 point (2)(a); wording 'only Article 6(1), Article 60a and Articles 102 to 112 shall apply' seen in the amending act. New Art. 2(13) also added (point (3)).
requirement_paraphrase: For high-risk AI related to Annex I Section B products, only Art. 6(1), Art. 60a and Arts. 102-112 apply; Arts. 57-59 apply only insofar as high-risk requirements are incorporated into the Section B legislation. Art. 2(13), new, lets specific requirements in Arts 9-15 and 17-25 be limited for Art. 6(1) systems where Section A law gives equivalent protection; delegated acts by 2 Aug 2027. Also note: the machinery reading depends on Annex I placement, which was not confirmed officially.

status_note: In force; high-risk obligations apply per B17
requirement_paraphrase: Deployers must assign trained, authorised human overseers, monitor operation against instructions, stop use and notify provider on risk, report serious incidents, and keep automatically generated logs at least six months.

status_note: Official: new subparagraph added to Art. 40(2); explorer's 'new paragraph 3' is not supported. Conflict resolved in favour of Orrick.
clause_or_section_seen: Art. 40(2) new subparagraph (2026/1744 point (17)); base Art. 40(1)-(3) not seen officially
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems following harmonised standards cited in the OJ are presumed to meet the matching Chapter III Section 2 requirements, only for what the standards cover.
